thread:
Aditya Rao: Kicking off a quick thread on PM-412 before we lock beta scope. Main question: do we ship Suggestions as read-only for beta, or include “apply” (even if guarded)? Also need to align on success metrics + what counts as “trusted” savings estimates.

Marissa Cole: Strong vote read-only for beta. The UI needs to build trust first, and “apply” opens up a whole rollback/guardrail surface area + permissions. We can still make it actionable via copy + links to config docs.

Dylan Brooks: +1 read-only for v0. “Apply” isn’t just UI; we need control plane mutation APIs, audit logging for changes, rollbacks, and QA coverage. That’s easily another sprint+.

Chris Osei: If we go read-only, can we be explicit in the PRD that beta success = usage + trust signals, not necessarily immediate realized savings? Need to set expectations with execs.

Jonas Weber: On “trusted” savings: we should define it as “directionally correct and stable within error bars,” not “guaranteed.” I’d propose: 
- has confidence interval
- shows baseline window + sample size
- no double counting across caching/batching
- telemetry freshness within threshold
If any of those fail, we either suppress or downgrade confidence.

Logan Wright: Telemetry freshness is the big one. If baselines are stale we’ll get week-to-week jumpiness and support tickets. We can gate display when baseline age > X hours (or label as stale).

Dev Patel: From Support POV, “apply” in beta will spike tickets. Even read-only, we’ll get “why did savings change” and “why no suggestions.” We need a crisp explanation pattern + canned responses.

Tessa Morgan: Design POV: showing an “Apply” button that’s disabled/coming soon is risky unless we’re super careful. It reads as “Redwood knows best but won’t let you do it.” I’d rather ship clean read-only with “How to implement” steps + a link to docs.

Rachel Kim: For enterprise cohort: they will ask for auditability. Even read-only, we should track: viewed/opened and when estimates were generated. If we do apply later, they’ll want “who changed what” + rollback story.

Aditya Rao: Totally. I’m getting pressure from GTM that “read-only” sounds weak, but I’d rather avoid regressions. What if we message it as “beta = recommendations + projected impact; apply via guided workflow (manual)”? (Phase 2 = one-click apply)

Marissa Cole: That works. In the drawer we can include: “Recommended change”, “Where it applies”, “Estimated savings”, “Risk level”, and “How to implement” (manual steps).

Dylan Brooks: If we do manual steps, we need to make sure we don’t accidentally imply it’s safe. Risk taxonomy needs to be prominent and consistent.

Jonas Weber: Re risk vs confidence: do we show both? I’m worried users will interpret “low risk” as “high confidence.” They’re correlated but not the same.

Aditya Rao: Yeah, that’s one of the decisions. My current leaning: show Risk (low/med/high) + “Estimate quality” / “Confidence” as a separate field (maybe a 0–100 or low/med/high). But that could overwhelm.

Tessa Morgan: We can do: primary chip = Risk. Secondary line item in “Basis of estimate” = “Confidence: Medium (based on N days of traffic, variance, etc)”. Keep the top of drawer clean.

Logan Wright: Please no 0–100. Everyone will debate calibration. If we must, keep it categorical with a deterministic rubric.

Chris Osei: Metrics: what are we optimizing for in beta? We need a KPI set we can actually measure in 8–10 weeks.

Aditya Rao: Proposed beta success metrics (rough):
1) Adoption: % of enabled workspaces that view Suggestions (at least 2 sessions)
2) Engagement: # suggestions opened per workspace, filter usage
3) “Trust”: users spend time on “Basis of estimate”, low rate of “this looks wrong” feedback
4) Outcome proxy: for customers who implement changes (manual), compare pre/post cost per 1M tokens (with caveats)

Rachel Kim: For enterprise CSMs, we also need “time-to-first-value”: time from enablement to first suggestion viewed + time to first config change.

Dev Patel: Add Support metric: # of tickets per enabled tenant and top issue categories. If it’s too noisy, we’re not ready for broader rollout.

Marissa Cole: +1. Also UI health metrics: empty state rate (how often we show “no suggestions” / “insufficient data”). If it’s >X% in the cohort, it’ll look broken.

Jonas Weber: “Trusted savings” definition should be in the PRD, not just implied. Suggest we define a “publish eligibility” gate for suggestions:
- baseline window >= 7 days OR token count >= threshold
- variance below threshold OR widen CI + mark as low confidence
- no missing telemetry fields
- no overlapping recs that double count
Only eligible suggestions get shown.

Logan Wright: We can implement most of that as part of the suggestions-service. But I want a visible “data window” displayed in UI so users understand why it changes.

Dylan Brooks: Re scope: read-only + telemetry events + feature flag + allowlist is already a lot. If we add “publish eligibility gates,” we should confirm effort. (But I agree it’s needed.)

Aditya Rao: Agree. The question is whether we *suppress* low-quality estimates or show them with warnings. Suppressing reduces confusion but increases “why no suggestions.”

Dev Patel: Please suppress if it’s truly unreliable. A warning label won’t stop “this number is wrong” tickets.

Tessa Morgan: We can do an “Insufficient data” empty state that’s specific: “We need at least 7 days of traffic on route X” / “Telemetry freshness issue.” That reduces mystery.

Marissa Cole: + we should not show a dollar number if we don’t have enough confidence. We can say “Potential savings detected; collecting more data” as a placeholder.

Jonas Weber: That’s good. “Potential savings” without a number is safer.

Chris Osei: Summarizing decisions for PM-412:
- Beta scope: read-only Suggestions list + detail drawer; no one-click apply
- Provide manual “how to implement” steps + docs links
- Success metrics: adoption/engagement, trust proxies, support load, and outcome proxy where possible
- Define “trusted savings” gates + show basis of estimate (data window, assumptions)
Can someone add this as a comment on PM-412?

Aditya Rao: I’ll update PM-412 with this thread summary + proposed KPI list. Also will add a section: “Trusted estimate criteria + suppression rules.”

Logan Wright: I’ll sanity check what we can instrument for “trust” (basis section views, time in drawer, etc). We should keep payload privacy-safe.

Marissa Cole: I’ll sync with Tessa on the drawer hierarchy and where to put confidence/basis so it doesn’t read like fine print.

Dev Patel: I’ll start a Support FAQ doc outline: “why risk is high,” “why savings changed,” “why no suggestions,” “what telemetry is required.”

Aditya Rao: Great. Last question: should we set a numeric bar for “trusted” in beta messaging? e.g., “estimates are within ±20% in offline validation”?

Jonas Weber: I’d avoid committing to a single % publicly. Internally, yes. Externally, say “estimates include confidence intervals and are based on your recent traffic; actual savings may vary.”

Rachel Kim: +1. Enterprises will hold us to any number we print.

Aditya Rao: Done. Read-only beta it is. I’ll post an updated PM-412 link when it’s in.

(Aditya Rao added a link) PM-412: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/PM-412
